tilts.set: SET on 2026-11-06 by the Portfolio Fitness for Fighting judg

industry.why: Neutral, carried, with the evidence moved towards the tape. Component 1 regime, 30-Oct-26 (risk-off beneath a steady index, led now by credit and the cost of debt rather than by the artificial intelligence wash-out alone: the US ten-year above 5% after a hawkish Fed hold with two dissents for a hike, Goldman Sachs' Risk Appetite Indicator at its lowest since April 2025, euro investment-grade and high-yield yields up 30 and 90 basis points since September, Brent near $115, the French premium a record 150 basis points, Europe rotating to quality, defensives and non-AI growth, the STOXX Europe 600 1.7% from its high with breadth recovering from the bottom fifth of three years and defensives leading cyclicals at four weeks and three months; sources present 2026-W44): third-quarter beats were sold (Sandvik down 5%, Atlas Copco down 8%, Hiab down 12%), Danske Bank's C-J (25 October) says 'a lot is priced in' with the order strength coming from data centres the market no longer pays for, and the exception is the non-AI compounder (Hexagon, 13% organic growth); against it, offshore services and nuclear have multi-year visibility and electrical equipment is still the physical bottleneck. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-30 against 2026-08-28, not week on week: D now, C prior. The sector rows do the work: Electrical equipment, Diversified groups, Distributors, Test and measurement and Engineered components at C, Flow control and Building technology at D. Five live holdings (19.35 points of the book) sit here, judged in component 4. Counter-case for D: a tape that sells beats is a regime statement; for B: the order data remain the strongest non-AI demand read in the pack. To D on a second week of beats sold with relative strength falling to F.

sector.why: Underweight, from Neutral. Component 1 regime, 16-Oct-26 (a discount-rate shock with the first credit crack inside the artificial intelligence chain: United States core inflation re-accelerating on energy, the Fed and Bank of England hikes pulled forward, the US 10-year about 5.1%, the US joined the sell-off and Asia is in washout, defensives bid for four weeks in Europe, European breadth off its three-year lows but in the bottom quarter, the consumer forecast to weaken into winter; sources present 2026-W42): the rate mechanism that set Construction contractors (M.6) and Cement and aggregates (M.10) at D last week reaches building products this week with a number: Goldman Sachs (13-Oct) estimate each 100 basis points of higher rates cuts developed-market housing investment 6%, Norway's Entra posted a large valuation loss, and construction customers were already postponing investment in last week's read. Relative strength per 31-relative-strength.md, 2026-10-16 against 2026-08-14, not week on week: D now, D prior, agrees. Counter-case: 26 stocks of mixed character, energy-efficiency retrofit demand benefits from the energy shock, British Land beat with 3 to 5% rental growth guidance, and rate-sensitive groups are where a relief rally starts; no MI Pool name sits in this row. Back to C if the Fed path is marked down.

geography.why: Neutral, carried; the re-test written last week (Neutral against Underweight after the Bank of England's decision and guidance on 5-Nov-26) could not run, because no source in the pack reports the outcome; the only United Kingdom items are undated headlines (the pound firmer on policy divergence; shoppers 'more upbeat than their European counterparts', City AM, against a GfK 'weakens in November' headline most likely from 2025). Component 1 regime, 6-Nov-26 (risk-off beneath an index at its high, now present in Europe's own prices: the STOXX Europe 600 0.9% from its 52-week high with the share of stocks above the 100, 150 and 200-day averages at or below the tenth percentile of near-high days since 2006, defensives leading cyclicals on all five windows, breadth recovering for a second week; the causes, inflation, rates, yields, credit and the consumer, unread this week because the strategist and newsletter files did not reach the pack, so the credit-and-cost-of-debt read of 30-Oct-26 with the US ten-year above 5% is held one week stale; sources present 2026-W45, headline-only). The Budget read of last week stands: a UK-specific fiscal tail risk removed without lowering the rate; 22 of the Pool stocks are UK-listed and a Neutral country carries no weight in Thematic Fit/Momentum. Counter-case unchanged: a 1.0% growth year with a hiking central bank is an Underweight in most books. To D on hawkish guidance when the 5-Nov-26 decision is read, a January price cap above 16% or a spring fiscal event with broad taxes; to B if a second source makes the UK case with the rate path read.

beta.method: Dimson: same-day plus previous-day market slopes, daily returns, last 252 common days, Stoxx Europe 600

experiment.label: Experiment
experiment.method: own daily moves (Stoxx Europe 600 and country-of-listing average removed), rank correlation, last 63 and 126 sessions; candidates EUR 500m or more in the same sector, cohort or country of listing

defs.atr: average true range: each day's high to low, stretched to the previous close on a gap, as a % of the previous close; L5D the last 5 sessions, L1M and L3M the last 30 and 91 calendar days
defs.top_half: a close above the midpoint of the day's high-low range; an up day closes at or above the previous close; days with no range are left out
